@sepo-agent /answer 

```
When an explicit `/implement` request on a pull request or discussion creates a tracking issue, the issue title is derived from the text after `/implement
``` 

This is not what i meant. The agent should generate a proper title for the issue given the description and the context.

You’re right. PR #232 implements the wrong behavior.

Current architecture explains why: explicit routes skip dispatch triage in [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L201-L241), then [`resolve-dispatch.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/resolve-dispatch.ts#L35-L55) uses deterministic metadata from [`buildRequestedRouteDecision`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/triage.ts#L94-L126). The tracking issue is then created from that `issue_title` in [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L589-L598).

The fix should not copy text after `/implement`. It should add a lightweight title/body generation step for explicit `/implement` on PRs/discussions, using the original mention plus target context, while still treating the slash command as explicit approval to run `agent-implement`.

Concrete revision plan:

1. Revert the command-tail title extraction in PR #232.
2. Add or reuse an agent prompt that generates only tracking issue metadata: concise title under 70 chars and structured issue body.
3. Run that metadata generation when `requested_route == implement` and the target is not already an issue.
4. Keep `needsApproval: false` for explicit `/implement`.
5. Keep `Implement requested change` only as an error/fallback path.
6. Add tests proving `/implement please fix this` does not literally become the title, and that PR/discussion context drives the generated metadata.

So the intended behavior is: `/implement` selects the route; the agent still synthesizes the issue title from the request and surrounding context.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #232 tries to fix issue #228, where explicit `/implement` requests from PR contexts create tracking issues with the unhelpful fallback title `Implement requested change`. The branch changes `.agent/src/triage.ts` so the title is built from text after `/implement`, adds triage tests for that behavior, and documents the new rule. The PR conversation later clarified that this is not the desired behavior: `/implement` should select the route, while Sepo should generate a proper tracking issue title from the request and surrounding context. The current branch therefore codifies the wrong product behavior even though it is small and well-tested.

## Review
The PR needs rework before merge. The independent reviews overlap on a parser flaw, but the current PR discussion adds a more fundamental blocker: literal command-tail title extraction is not what the requester intended.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Command-tail titles implement the wrong behavior | BLOCKING | [`triage.ts#L136`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4a18637a35667ffa16e68bf3ba50897f371b31a4/.agent/src/triage.ts#L136), the tests, and [`supported-workflows.md#L213`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4a18637a35667ffa16e68bf3ba50897f371b31a4/.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md#L213) now make the issue title come from text after `/implement`. The requester clarified that Sepo should synthesize a proper title from the description and context instead. |
| Command detail parsing is not tied to the live mention | WARNING | [`explicitRouteRequestDetail`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4a18637a35667ffa16e68bf3ba50897f371b31a4/.agent/src/triage.ts#L47) scans for the first bare `/implement` in the sanitized request, not the validated `@sepo-agent /implement` command. If any command-detail extraction remains, prose that mentions `/implement` before the actual command can drive the wrong metadata. |

## Progress
- Issue #228 and the original answer-only diagnosis identified the weak fallback title and proposed deriving a title from command text.
- The requester clarified in PR #232 that command-tail copying is not the intended behavior; the agent response acknowledged that the PR implements the wrong behavior and outlined a generation-based revision plan.
- Rubrics review passed overall but flagged the same mention-anchoring concern as a partial reuse/structured-input gap.
- No new inline comments, replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed: there are no existing inline comments/threads, and the core product mismatch plus parser concern are already covered in the PR discussion.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Command-tail titles implement the wrong behavior</summary>

**Cause:** The implementation keeps explicit `/implement` deterministic by deriving `issueTitle` from `originalRequest` text after the slash command. That locks in the behavior the requester rejected: `/implement please fix this` can become the tracking issue title instead of using the PR/discussion context to generate a concise task title.

**Candidate solutions:** Replace command-tail title derivation with a lightweight metadata generation step for explicit `/implement` on PRs/discussions. Keep `/implement` as explicit route approval, preserve the generic fallback only for generation failure or missing usable metadata, and update tests/docs to assert generated context-derived metadata rather than literal command text.

**Comments:** Claude treated the first-occurrence parser issue as non-blocking under the earlier inferred design, while Codex and rubrics flagged it more strongly. After the requester clarification, the command-tail design itself is the blocker.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Command detail parsing is not tied to the live mention</summary>

**Cause:** `extractRequestedRouteDecision` validates `@sepo-agent /implement`, but `explicitRouteRequestDetail` re-scans the full request for any `/implement`. A body like `The /implement path is weak. @sepo-agent /implement add retry handling` can extract from the prose occurrence instead of the live command.

**Candidate solutions:** Prefer removing this parser as part of the generation-based fix. If any command detail remains an input, derive it from the same mention-qualified match used for route selection and add a regression where an earlier bare `/implement` is ignored.

**Comments:** This issue is likely subsumed by replacing literal command-tail extraction, but it should stay guarded if the revised implementation still parses command text.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The requester has clarified the intended behavior, and the remaining work is a concrete branch change that an automated fix-pr pass can safely apply with tests and docs.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Replace literal text-after-`/implement` title derivation with context-derived issue metadata generation for explicit `/implement` tracking issues, while preserving explicit route approval and the generic fallback path.
- [ ] Update tests and documentation so they assert generated context-based titles and guard against earlier prose `/implement` mentions driving metadata.

**Candidate solutions:** Optionally scope `explicit_dispatch` to implement-only, and either enforce the title length in `normalizeImplementIssueMetadata` or leave truncation centralized in `create-issue.ts`.

**Comments:** These are cleanup notes, not required branch changes for this PR.

Both PRs now aim at the right product behavior: explicit `/implement` still selects the route, while a metadata-only agent pass generates the tracking issue title/body from PR or discussion context.

Key differences:

| Area | #232 | #236 | Better |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access policy before metadata generation | Resolves explicit route authorization first, then runs metadata only if route is authorized `implement` | Runs metadata generation based on raw `requested_route == implement` before dispatch policy resolution | **#232** |
| Metadata agent permissions | Uses `permission_mode: approve-reads` | Uses `permission_mode: approve-all` | **#232** |
| Metadata schema | Prompt returns only `issue_title` and `issue_body`; parser validates those fields | Prompt returns a full dispatch-shaped object including `route`, `needs_approval`, `summary`, `confidence` | **#232**, narrower contract |
| Route safety | Generated metadata cannot change the route by shape | Generated response is normalized as dispatch output, then route mismatch is ignored | #236 has a guard, but #232 avoids the risk earlier |
| Fallback behavior | Invalid/missing generated metadata falls back to generic implement metadata | Invalid/mismatched generated metadata falls back too | Tie |
| Docs/tests coverage | Broader: request lifecycle docs, supported workflows docs, triage tests, resolve-dispatch tests, workflow contract test | Good but narrower; lacks request-lifecycle update and uses approve-all in workflow test | **#232** |

The biggest concern in #236 is this line in its workflow diff: the metadata generation step uses `permission_mode: approve-all`. Since that prompt only needs to read context and emit JSON, #232’s `approve-reads` is the safer design.

I would merge or continue with #232, not #236. #236 is conceptually aligned, but it looks like an earlier/parallel implementation that missed the later hardening done on #232.

You’re right to push on this. The later gate cannot be reused as a **single workflow step** because of an ordering dependency.

Current desired flow is:

```text
extract context
→ decide whether explicit /implement is authorized enough to run metadata prompt
→ run metadata prompt
→ final resolve-dispatch using generated metadata
→ create issue / dispatch implement
```

The later `Resolve route` step needs the metadata prompt output:

```yaml
RESPONSE_FILE: ${{ steps.triage.outputs.response_file || steps.implement_metadata.outputs.response_file }}
```

So if we tried to use only the later gate, we get a cycle:

```text
Need final Resolve route to know whether metadata prompt is allowed.
Need metadata prompt output before final Resolve route can produce final issue_title/body.
```

That is why the PR adds an earlier precheck. It is not a separate auth model; it is an early call to the same policy machinery so the metadata prompt does not run before authorization.

Could we restructure to avoid this shape? Yes, but it would be more awkward:

1. Run `resolve-dispatch.js` early with fallback metadata.
2. Run metadata prompt if authorized.
3. Run another merge/finalize step to replace fallback title/body.

That still has two phases; it just moves the duplication around.

So the honest answer is: **we can reuse the same code, but not the same later workflow step**, because the later step depends on metadata that has not been generated yet. The current approach is reasonable if the precheck is narrowly scoped and clearly named as a metadata precheck.
